steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook garlic in butter briefly. Stir in wine and season with oregano, parsley, and red pepper flakes.
Place clams in wine mixture. Cover and steam until all clams have opened, about 5-7 minutes. Discard any that do not open. Serve in soup bowls and ladle broth generously over them.

raw_recipe.headline: Clams Italiano
raw_recipe.description: These Italian clams are steamed in wine, butter, and spices and are the perfect addition to any dinner party. Savor the broth by dipping bread in it.
raw_recipe.name: Clams Italiano

review.reviewBody: YUM! The family really liked this for our 7 fish deast on Christmas Eve. HINT: Once you scrub the clams, put them in a bowl of cold water and sprinkle 1 T corn meal over them. Let them sit for half and hour then rinse and cook. This cornmeal "snack" feeds them and they spit out any sand they have inside in favor of the cornmeal. Learned this trick from Cooking Light.

I’ve learned from Rick Moonem to steam clams separately in cup of wine and splash of water remove them as they JUST open , set aside , strain the juice in fine strainer lined with cheese cloth. then sauté garlic, shallots, butter, more wine, etc Add clams to heat. Great flavor, no grit.

I loved this recipe. I could only get a dozen little neck clams so I added a half dozen Argentinian shrimp and cut the recipe back to two servings which is great for two appy's or a meal for one. Crusty bread is a must so I made Ciabatta Bread , the recipe is by Marina and on this site. After cleaning the clams I placed them in a bowl of water and added a good sprinkling of corn mean that the clams will ingest, something that my Dad always did. This will result in the clams releasing any sand that may be in the shell. I cooked these for four minutes, shaking the pan occasionally. Great recipe, thanks for sharing.

Delicious - delicate tasting but full of flavor. I halved the broth ingredients as I was using smaller clams (pre-shelled when hubby caught them), and I added a few frozen julienned carrots and some sliced mushrooms to the broth about 4 or 5 minutes before taking off the stove. Next time I think I may reduce the oregano a bit like another reviewer suggested.

This is a fantastic recipe! I usually serve this dish over linguine, but most recently, I cooked the clams and sauce in a large foil pan on the grill and served it with crusty Italian bread as an appetizer. Received many compliments. And you can freeze the leftover sauce for another meal -- just add some fresh clams.

I put the butter, garlic, oregano, crushed red pepper, and 50 Little Necks, 1 cup white cooking wine, one cup chicken broth, 2 tsp of basil and two cans of stewed tomatoes which I chopped up with a potatoe masher and these where DELICIOUS!!

Overall the recipe as is is a good starting block. I added a little more garlic and red pepper flake, tsp of salt and pepper, some basil and diced onoin. Also, I did not use 2 full cups of wine (Pinot Grigio). Instead I used a small can of minced clams with it's juice and filled the can twice with white wine (approximately 1 cup). I also added some diced potato. It was pretty darn good. Great for dipping bread, and the potato added a little substance so it could be eaten as a soup as well.

Actually, my boyfriend made this for my birthday dinner a few months ago. It turned out great, except that he didn't know you're supposed to soak the clams before cooking so they release all the sand and other grossness...I feel that should be added to the recipe instructions for newer cooks!

Otherwise, great recipe as-is.

This is a good recipe but the wine was just too much and overpowering for us. I made it again the next day because we just all love clams and instead of 2 cups of wine, I used only 1 and used 1 1/2 cups of chicken stock. 36 clams for 6 people is also not realistic. Between 3 people, we easily had 4 pounds of clams (which was way more than 36) and could have had more.

My son and his girlfriend came to dinner last night. I wanted to make something a little "different" for them, so following many of the suggestions by other posters, we had this dish in its main course form with 5 lb of mahogany clams. I reduced the wine by half, replacing it with chicken broth and used 3 T of grated garlic. This one goes into permanent record!

I've made this recipe many, many times for friends and family and it's always wonderful. I live in the Pacific Northwest where clams are plentiful on the beaches so trying to find different ways to prepare them is fun. The only thing I do differently in this recipe is use a lot more clams than the recipe calls for, I cook them in batches since they won't all fit into my pan and I just keep adding more to the same broth as the others cook and are removed. I also use fresh parsley since we never seem to have dried ones and instead of wine, we use chicken broth like someone else suggested.
only added lemon. great recipe
I first made this recipe 15 years ago! Still love it till today and this recipe alone converted my husband to a clam lover.
This recipe is fantastic
Made my 7 Fishes Christmas Eve Dinner complete. My favorite part of the meal.
Been making this for a few years now and it’s always a hit!
can't go wrong with this recipe, great flavors!
My husband devoured his clams and wished he had more! Great recipe as is with no changes! Thanks! ( I used a Pinot Grigio for the wine)
Outstanding!

This was really good as is. I used fresh herbs and added basil, but I think it would have been just as good without the addition. My kids ate this, and even my husband, who's even pickier than the kids, ate this. I served this over homemade noodles and sprinkled with Parmesan cheese. Will absolutely make this again!
